parameters.name: actor

The posted form is bounded to 512 KiB before it is parsed, and a body over that bound is answered 401 login-failed with the flow left a tombstone. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so an assertion is handled at most once. Without a flow cookie the route serves an identity-provider-initiated sign-in, but only for an enterprise provider whose row enables it.

parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

get.description: Answers every factor row the caller's account has registered, ordered oldest first by creation time and then by identifier. Each row carries the kind, label, lifecycle status and the instants it was created, activated and last used; it carries no seed, key, public key or other data a kind keeps for itself. The list is empty when the account has registered none.

200.description: The caller's factors, without any seed, key or other secret of a kind's own

schema.description: An object whose single member lists every factor the caller's account has registered.

delete.description: Removes one factor of the caller's account: whatever the factor's kind keeps for it is removed first, then its register row. The call requires a fresh multi-factor authentication verified locally, so one merely declared by an identity provider does not satisfy it; an impersonating identity is refused. A factor that is not the caller's answers the same as one already gone, so the route never answers 404 and repeating a removal is idempotent. When the account has mfa_required set, its last active factor cannot be removed.

post.description: Starts a login flow for the method named in the body and advances it through the method's first step. The flow token is written to the flow cookie, or, with `binding` set to `header`, returned in `flow_token` with no cookie; later calls are bound to the flow by that token. The route reads no cookie, so a stale session cookie does not prevent a login. Depending on the method and the multi-factor policy, the returned flow may already stand at a second-factor, enrollment or ready step. A body that is not `application/json` is a 415, an unknown member or a value outside its domain is a 400, and a credential the method did not accept is a 401 login-failed — except two refusals the route answers as a 400: a phone prefix the deployment does not allow (`unsupported-region`) and an identifier that cannot name an account (`bad-request`). A 429 carries `Retry-After` when the back-off states a delay.

requestBody.description: The start request: the method to run, how the flow token is carried, where to return after a completed login, and the fields the method's first step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

schema.description: The start request; `method` must name a login method this deployment takes in, or the call is a bad request.

method.description: The stable name of a login method, as returned in `name` by `GET /auth/methods`. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request; a method turned off by the deployment is a 403 method-disabled.

purpose.description: Accepted but not read by this route: a flow started here always has the purpose login. Use `POST /auth/flows/authenticated` for link, step-up or enroll.

delivery.description: How a completed login is delivered: `session` (the default) sets the session cookie and answers the session view; `token` answers an access and refresh token pair. `token` must be enabled by the deployment and requires the token capability, otherwise the request is a 400 bad-request.

return_to.description: Where to send the user agent after a callback login completes: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts. Anything else is a 400 bad-request. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`, or `authn-flow` when insecure use is allowed) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

post.description: Advances the flow the request is bound to by one step. The body must echo the flow's current `seq`, or the call is a 401 flow-invalid. `step` must be one of `answer`, `factor`, `enroll` or `complete`: a name outside that set is a 400 bad-request, and a step the flow's state does not accept is a 401 flow-invalid. A flow accepts at most eight client answers, after which it is moved to failed and every later answer is a 401 flow-invalid. The answer is the flow at its next step or, once the flow is ready, the completed result: the session view, the token pair, or the `linked`/`enrolled` result of a link or enrollment. Each step is a compare-and-swap on the flow record, so concurrent answers are decided by the store and the loser gets 401 flow-invalid rather than a retry.

requestBody.description: One answer to the bound flow: the step number to echo, the step being answered, and the fields that step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

seq.description: The `seq` of the flow as last returned. It must equal the record's current step number; a stale or future value is a 401 flow-invalid.

step.description: The step being answered: `answer` for a first-factor submission, only while the flow is at the first factor; `factor` for a second-factor step, only at the second factor; `enroll` for an enrollment step, only at the enroll state; `complete` to take the result of a ready flow. A name outside this set is a 400 bad-request, and a step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid.

input.description: The fields the step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 8 KiB; a second-factor step reads `factor` to choose the factor and then the values that factor asks for, an enrollment step reads `kind`, and `complete` reads nothing.

post.description: Starts a `link`, `step-up` or `enroll` flow on the identity the gateway authenticated and advances it to its first step. The flow is bound to that account and session, and an impersonating identity is refused with 403 impersonation-restricted. A link and an enrollment require the fresh authentication the account's factors call for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise — and answer 401 insufficient_user_authentication with `WWW-Authenticate` when it does not hold. A step-up whose account holds at least one factor usable for this session starts at the second factor and answers the offered factors without calling the method; an account that holds factors but none usable for this session — because each was activated at or after the session authenticated — is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication, and an account with no factor starts at the first factor with the method named in the body. The delivery mode is not read from the body: it follows the kind of the request's session.

A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request.

purpose.description: Required, and one of `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`: bind an external identity, strengthen the current session, or register a factor. Any other value, including an empty one, is a 400 bad-request.

A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

post.description: Adds one login identifier to the caller's account. `kind=username` writes a login name at once, recorded as the account's own assertion; `kind=email` sends a code to the address and answers `state: pending` with how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, and the address is written only after `POST /auth/identifiers/verify` accepts the code. A second code to the same normalized address within the resend interval is a 429 throttled; the window is held against the address and shared across sessions and accounts. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for and refuses an impersonating identity; a write rotates the caller's session token and revokes the account's other sessions. A login name or address another account holds is a 409 conflict, and a deployment with no email channel answers the email branch with 503 unavailable.

value.description: The login name or address to add. A username is NFKC-normalized and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is 3 to 64 characters of [a-z0-9._-] beginning with a letter or a digit and does not carry the reserved static-credential prefix; the stored value is the normalized one. An email address is trimmed and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is ASCII, contains exactly one `@` with no whitespace, and is at most 254 bytes; anything else is a 400 bad-request.

post.description: Accepts the code sent to an email address being added and, on a match, writes the address as an identifier verified by that code. The pending address and the code's digest are read from the server-side record of the caller's session, so the client submits only the code and cannot choose which address is verified. A missing record, one that names another account, or one that does not parse is a 401 flow-invalid. A wrong code is a 401 login-failed; five wrong codes for one issued code spend the pending verification, and the record also expires with the code's lifetime. On success the record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 200 with `state: added`.

code.description: The six-digit code the email channel delivered, as a string. Empty or longer than 32 bytes is a 400 bad-request; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed, and five wrong codes for one issued code spend the pending verification.

delete.description: Removes one login identifier the caller's account holds. The identifier must be the caller's own: one that does not exist and one that belongs to another account are answered identically as a 400 bad-request, so the route discloses nothing about what another account holds. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for and refuses an impersonating identity. The route does not check whether the identifier is the account's last way to sign in, so the last one can be removed; that rule belongs to unbinding an external identity. Unlike the routes that add a way in, this one does not revoke the caller's other sessions, and it publishes no event of its own: `authn.identifier.changed` is published by the account module on the removal.

delete.description: Ends the unended record on the caller's session with the reason explicit, whether or not it is still valid, and answers 204. Repeating it is safe: once the record is ended a further call answers 404. Under a cookie credential the impersonation marker is cleared from the session without rotating its token, so the caller continues as its own identity; a failed audit write does not undo the end.

A cookie credential receives the record only and has the impersonation marker set on its session; a bearer credential also receives an impersonation access token whose lifetime is the shorter of the access-token setting and the record's remaining lifetime.

The binding must be the caller's own; one that is not, whether it does not exist or belongs to another account, is a 400 bad-request. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for — a multi-factor assurance merely declared by an identity provider does not count — and refuses an impersonating identity. post.description: Revokes the session the request's credential belongs to and writes a Set-Cookie header that has the browser drop the session cookie. When the identity is impersonating, the session revoked is the administrator's own, the one the credential belongs to, so the impersonation ends with it. A repeated call from the same credential is answered 401 on the replica that revoked the session, which clears its verification cache as it revokes. Another replica can still accept it while its own check cache holds (check-ttl, five seconds by default), unless the revocation event clears that entry first; such a call is answered 204, and it clears that replica's cache too, so a further call there is 401 as well.

On success the current session is rotated to a new token, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204 with the new session cookie set. An account that has neither a username nor a verified email is refused with 409 login-identifier-required.

post.description: Sends a verification code to a phone number the caller wants to add to the account, and answers how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, both in whole seconds. The answer carries no challenge identifier and no hint whether the number already belongs to another account: a number another account holds is sent a code exactly as a free one is, and the conflict surfaces only when the verified number is written. The pending verification is held against the caller's session, so one session has at most one and a later call replaces it. The route is present only in an assembly that takes in the SMS code capability. A key-value store that cannot be read is a 503 before any code is sent; a store that cannot be written after the code went out is also a 503, and the code then cannot be verified.

post.description: Verifies the code sent to the pending number and binds that number to the caller's account as an identifier verified by SMS code, replacing a phone the account already has. The number and the challenge are taken from the server-side record of the caller's session, not from the request, so a client cannot choose which number is verified. The number's back-off is checked before the code is compared, so a number in back-off answers 429 without offering the code to a guess; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed and counts against the number, and a correct one clears the back-off. On success the pending record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204. A missing pending record, or one that names another account, is a 401 flow-invalid.

get.description: Returns the SAML 2.0 service provider entity descriptor that the identity provider side is registered against, as XML. The entityID is this metadata address itself, so each provider sees a distinct service provider; the assertion consumer service points at the engine's callback route for the same provider with the HTTP-POST binding, WantAssertionsSigned is true, and AuthnRequestsSigned follows the provider's sign_requests setting. A success carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`; failures carry the RFC 6749 §5.2 body whose only member is `error`, with no `error_description`, and are never problem+json.

post.description: The RFC 7009 revocation endpoint. The body is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, capped at 8 KiB, and its only read field is `token`. The answer is 200 with an empty body whatever the token's state — valid, invalid, unknown, or a body that cannot be read — so a presenter cannot use the endpoint to probe whether a token exists. A refresh token revokes the session it belongs to, an ordinary access token whose signature holds revokes its `sid`'s session, an impersonation token ends its record and leaves the administrator's session alone, and a service access token is a no-op. Only a dependency that cannot answer gives 503 `temporarily_unavailable`, in the RFC 6749 §5.2 body, rather than reporting a revocation that did not happen.

allow_sha1.description: True when SHA-1 signed assertions are accepted; the route then warns about the downgrade.

merge_existing.description: True when just-in-time sign-up may merge into an existing account; the route then warns about it.

config.description: The protocol's own configuration; absent when the provider carries none

version.description: The provider's version, raised by every write.

warnings.description: Absent when no setting loosens a default

AuthnAdminProviderEnvelope.description: A response carrying one SSO provider.

AuthnAdminProviderList.description: The SSO providers of one tenant.

providers.description: The tenant's providers; the empty array when it has none.

AuthnAdminProviderWrite.description: The request that creates or replaces an SSO provider. Booleans left out keep their stored value on an update and are false on a create, and config is required either way.

tenant.description: Absent on a create takes the path's tenant; a value that names another is refused

protocol.description: The protocol: oidc or saml. The set is closed.

name.description: The provider's display name; 1 to 64 characters.

enabled.description: Absent leaves the enabled flag as it is (false on a create)

provisioning.description: jit creates an account on first sign-in; preprovisioned matches only an account an administrator has already created. Required, with no default.

trust_idp_mfa.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

allow_idp_initiated.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

allow_sha1.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

merge_existing.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

client_secret.description: Absent writes no client secret on a create and keeps the stored one on an update

AuthnAdminRemoved.description: The number of factors a multi-factor reset removed.

AuthnAdminRevoked.description: The number of sessions a bulk revocation ended.

AuthnAdminSecret.description: One service secret as the listing shows it: identifier, label, expiry and revocation state, never the secret value.

id.description: The secret's identifier, not the secret value.

label.description: The label given to the secret when it was created.

expires_at.description: When the secret expires, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; the zero instant 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z means it never expires.

revoked.description: True when the secret has been revoked.

AuthnAdminSecretCreate.description: The request that mints a service secret.

label.description: The label for the administrator's own reference: at most 100 bytes of valid UTF-8 with no control character.

expires_at.description: Absent mints a secret with no expiry

AuthnAdminSecretCreated.description: A freshly minted service secret. The secret value appears in this response only.

id.description: The new secret's identifier.

label.description: The label given in the request.

secret.description: The secret itself, handed out once and never again

expires_at.description: The zero instant 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z when the request named no expiry

AuthnAdminSecretList.description: The service secrets of one account, oldest first.

secrets.description: The account's service secrets, oldest first; the empty array when it has none.

AuthnAdminSession.description: One session of an account, without any credential a caller could use to take it over.

id.description: The session's opaque identifier.

kind.description: The session kind: browser for a cookie session, token for an access and refresh token pair.

auth_time.description: When the session last authenticated, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

impersonation_id.description: Absent unless the session carries an impersonation

created_at.description: When the session was created, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

last_seen_at.description: When a request last used the session, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

expires_at.description: The session's absolute expiry, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

revoked.description: True when the session has been revoked.

current.description: True when the row is the caller's own session

AuthnAdminSessionList.description: The live sessions of one account, most recently created first.

sessions.description: The account's live browser and token sessions, most recently created first; the empty array when it has none.

AuthnAdminVerifyToken.description: The token to publish in DNS to verify a claimed domain.

verify_token.description: The token to publish in DNS

AuthnImpersonationGrant.description: An impersonation record as a client sees it. The reason and the administrator's identity are not part of it.

id.description: Identifier of the impersonation record, minted when the start was granted.

tenant.description: The tenant the impersonation is confined to

started_at.description: Absent on the answer to a start, present on a record in force

ends_at.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the record stops being valid; never more than one hour after it began.

AuthnImpersonationGrantEnvelope.description: The answer of the status route.

grant.description: The record in force on the session, including the instant it began.

AuthnImpersonationStart.description: The answer of a start: the record just created and, for a bearer credential, the impersonation access token.

grant.description: The record just created; started_at is absent because a start answer does not carry the start instant.

access_token.description: Present on a bearer start; absent on a cookie start, whose carrier is the session cookie

expires_in.description: Present with access_token; the access token's lifetime in whole seconds

account.description: Identifier of the account the membership belongs to: an existing account or one created by this acceptance.

tenant.description: The string form of the tenant identifier the membership was written in.

active.description: Whether the membership is active; an acceptance always writes an active one.

source.description: The membership's source; an acceptance always writes invite.

sso_exempt.description: Whether the membership is exempt from SSO enforcement; an acceptance writes false.

AuthnInviteInvitation.description: One invitation as the management face shows it. It never carries the acceptance token.

id.description: The invitation's opaque identifier, used to revoke it.

tenant.description: The string form of the tenant identifier the invitation grants a membership in.

status.description: The stored state. Expiry is not stored: an expired pending invitation still reads pending.

invited_by.description: The account identifier of the issuer; empty when a host command issued the invitation without an HTTP identity.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline in UTC; a pending invitation at or past it can no longer be accepted.

accepted_at.description: The zero instant 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z when the invitation has not been accepted

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of issuance.

AuthnInviteIssued.description: The answer of an issue: the invitation's view together with its one-time acceptance token.

invitation.description: The issued invitation; the token is delivered beside it, not inside it.

token.description: The acceptance token, handed out once

AuthnInvitePage.description: One page of a tenant's invitations together with the cursor of the next page.

invitations.description: The invitations of this page, ordered by status ascending (pending, accepted, revoked) and then newest first with the identifier as the tie-break.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, empty on the last page

AuthnInviteView.description: The answer of the acceptance read: the invitation a token points to.

invitation.description: The invitation the token points to, without its token.

AuthnLoginActionResult.description: The answer of a flow that finished by binding an external identity (`linked`) or registering a factor (`enrolled`); neither issues a session or a token.

state.description: linked when the flow bound an external identity; enrolled when it registered a factor

AuthnLoginFactor.description: One second factor the flow offers to verify: its identifier, its kind and a display label. It carries nothing secret.

id.description: The factor's identifier; send it as `input.factor` when answering the second-factor step.

kind.description: The factor kind, such as `totp`, `sms` or `webauthn`; the client renders the challenge according to it.

label.description: A display label for the factor; it may be empty, in which case the client falls back to the kind's own name.

AuthnLoginField.description: One input a method asks the client for, named by the method and rendered according to its kind.

name.description: The input's key: the client submits its value under this name in the `input` map of the start request or of the answer.

kind.description: How the client renders the input: `text`, `password`, `code` or `phone`.

required.description: Whether the step needs a value; absent means the field may be left out.

secret.description: Whether the value must not be displayed or echoed, as for a password or a code; absent means it is not secret.

AuthnLoginFlow.description: One open login flow, as returned by a start, by an answer that keeps the flow open, or by the current-flow read: the step number the next answer must echo, the flow's state, the flow token when the flow is bound by the header, and what the client does next.

seq.description: The step number the next answer must echo

state.description: The flow's state: first, second, enroll, ready, processing, done or failed

flow_token.description: The flow token, set only when the flow is bound by the Authn-Flow header

next.description: What the client does at the flow's current step.

AuthnLoginIdentifierState.description: The answer of adding an identifier: `added` when the identifier is written, `pending` when a code was sent to an email address and the answer is still to come. The two durations are present only in the pending state.

state.description: added when the identifier is written; pending when a code was sent to an address and its answer is still to come

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds; absent when the state is added

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds; absent when the state is added

AuthnLoginMFA.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, as the multi-factor module reports them. This is a deployment-level list, not the caller's own registered factors.

factors.description: The kinds of second factor the deployment takes in

AuthnLoginMethods.description: The discovery document of the login surface: one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off, whether a first login may open an account, and the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

methods.description: The methods taking part that are not turned off, one descriptor each, sorted by name

signup.description: Whether a first login may open an account on this deployment.

mfa.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in.

AuthnLoginPhoneChallenge.description: The answer to a phone-verification send: how long the code lives and how soon another code may be asked for, both in whole seconds. It carries neither the challenge identifier nor any fact about whether the number is already held by another account.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds

AuthnLoginSession.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=session`, and of a step-up completed on a cookie session: the state name `authenticated` and the public facts of the session that was created or elevated. The session cookie is set in the same response.

state.description: The literal `authenticated`, marking a completed login.

session.description: The public facts of the session the login created.

AuthnLoginSessionView.description: The public facts of the session a login created. No token or secret is included.

id.description: The session identifier; the browser client holds the session cookie written in the same response.

expires_at.description: The session's expiry as an RFC 3339 instant, or empty

AuthnLoginSignup.description: Whether a first login may open an account on this deployment, derived from the account module's signup switch. A closed switch does not remove a method; it only makes a first login for an unknown identifier fail.

enabled.description: Whether a first login may open an account

AuthnLoginStep.description: What the client does at the flow's current step. Only the members that belong to `kind` are present: `challenge` carries `fields`; `redirect` carries `url` and `method`; `factor` carries `factors`; `enroll` carries `kinds`; `webauthn` carries `options`; `complete` carries nothing.

kind.description: What the client does next: challenge, redirect, factor, enroll, complete or webauthn

fields.description: The inputs a challenge step asks for

expires_in.description: How long a challenge lives, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

resend_after.description: How soon a challenge may be asked for again, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

url.description: Where a redirect step sends the user agent

method.description: The HTTP method the redirect uses

factors.description: The factors a second-factor step offers

kinds.description: The factor kinds an enroll step takes in

options.description: The data a webauthn step carries: the public-key creation or request options of a WebAuthn ceremony, or, for a TOTP enrollment, an object with an `otpauth_uri` the client renders as a QR code.

AuthnLoginToken.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=token`, and of a token-delivered step-up: the state name, the token type, the access token, its lifetime and the refresh token.

state.description: authenticated for a login; elevated for a step-up, which issues no refresh token and carries it empty

token_type.description: The authorization scheme the access token is sent with; it is always `Bearer`.

access_token.description: The access token, sent in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <value>`.

expires_in.description: The access token's lifetime in seconds

refresh_token.description: Empty on a step-up, which issues no refresh token

AuthnMethodDescriptor.description: One login method as the discovery document reports it: its stable name, how a client renders it, the protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks, its brand label, whether it can open an account, and the inputs its first step asks for.

kind.description: How a client renders the method: form, redirect, enterprise or webauthn

protocol.description: The wire protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks: oauth2, oidc or saml; empty otherwise

label.description: The method's brand name where it has one, otherwise empty for a name-keyed translation

opens_account.description: Whether the method may open an account for an identifier it does not yet know

fields.description: The inputs the method's first step asks for, empty for a method that does not open with a form

AuthnMfaFactor.description: One factor row of the caller's account: what the register holds about the factor, with nothing a kind keeps for itself.

id.description: The factor's identifier; use it as the `id` path parameter of `DELETE /auth/factors/{id}`.

label.description: The display label stored with the factor; this module writes an empty label when it registers one.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `pending` is registered but not yet confirmed and is never used to verify, `active` may verify, and `disabled` (left by an administrator reset or a clone warning) stays as a row that no longer counts.

created_at.description: When the factor row was created, as an RFC 3339 instant

activated_at.description: When the factor became active, as an RFC 3339 instant; absent until it is

last_used_at.description: When the factor last passed a verification, as an RFC 3339 instant; absent until it first does

AuthnProfileIdentifier.description: One identifier bound to the account, with the way its ownership was established.

id.description: The identifier's own identifier

kind.description: The identifier kind: username, email or phone

value.description: The identifier's value in the normalized form the account module stores: a username lower-cased, an email address trimmed and lower-cased, a phone number in E.164 with a leading plus sign and 7 to 15 digits

verified_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, the instant the identifier's ownership was established; always present, as no identifier is stored awaiting verification

verified_via.description: How the identifier's ownership was established: sms-code, email-code, invite, idp:<provider> (followed by the provider's identifier), admin, import-unverified or self. The first four prove ownership; admin, import-unverified and self only record a fact an administrator, an import or the account's own holder asserted

AuthnProfileLink.description: One external identity bound to the account, as the account module keeps it; it carries no provider subject.

id.description: The binding's own identifier

provider.description: The provider the binding was made through, as the provider is registered

email.description: Absent when the provider gave no address

created_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, empty when the binding carries no creation instant

last_login_at.description: Absent when the binding has never been used to sign in

AuthnProfilePatch.description: The self-writable fields as they stand after a profile write, read back from what was stored.

display_name.description: The display name as it stands after the write; the account's current one when the body carried none

attributes.description: The whole attribute set as it stands, never null

locale.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

time_zone.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

AuthnProfileProfile.description: The caller's own profile: the account's self fields plus its identifiers and external bindings, which this surface only reads. It is built field by field from the account module's values, so a field added to the record there does not reach a client by being there.

account_id.description: The account's identifier, the one the request's identity names; never empty on a 200.

kind.description: The account's kind: user or service, a service being a non-interactive API client.

display_name.description: The account's display name, empty when it carries none

mfa_required.description: Whether the account must register a factor

password_set.description: Whether the account has a password credential set

created_at.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, empty when the account carries no creation instant

attributes.description: Never null; the empty object when the account carries none

locale.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

time_zone.description: Read out of the attribute set, empty when it carries none

identifiers.description: The account's identifiers; always an array, never null, and empty when the account has none

links.description: The account's external bindings; always an array, never null, and empty when there are none. The provider's own subject for the person is not included

AuthnSessionItem.description: One live session of the caller's, as the listing reports it.

id.description: The public session identifier; it names the row and is not a credential.

kind.description: The session kind, browser or token; service-account sessions are never listed.

created_at.description: When the session was created, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

last_seen_at.description: Last activity of the session, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. For a browser session this is the last use the row was written for: touches are coalesced, written at most once per effective touch interval — the configured interval capped at half the idle timeout — so the value lags the newest use by up to that interval. A token session has no renewal path, so its value is the creation time.

expires_at.description: The absolute expiry, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC. A browser session can stop being valid earlier, once its idle timeout passes.

client_ip.description: Empty when the session carries none

user_agent.description: Empty when the session carries none

current.description: Whether this is the session the request came with

AuthnSessionList.description: The caller's own live sessions, in the order the listing reports them.

sessions.description: The live browser and token sessions of the account, most recently created first; the empty array when there are none.

AuthnSessionRevoked.description: The outcome of revoking every session of the caller's but the current one.

AuthnSessionView.description: Whether the request carries a signed-in identity and, when it does, the facts the identity is built from.

authenticated.description: False when nobody is signed in; every other field is then absent

session_id.description: The public identifier of the session the request came with; absent when nobody is signed in.

account_id.description: The account the request is taken to be from; the impersonated account while impersonating

actor_id.description: The account whose hands are on the request; present only while impersonating

impersonating.description: True only while the identity is impersonating another account; absent otherwise.

methods.description: The authentication methods the identity completed, each from the closed set named by the enum; absent when the session records none.

assurance.description: The assurance level the authentication reached; "none" when the identity carries no level.

auth_time.description: The instant of the last interactive authentication, absent when the identity carries none

provider.description: The backend that verified the credential

AuthnSsoProvider.description: One SSO sign-in entry a client can offer for a domain. It carries only public identity; no endpoint, configuration or secret is exposed.

id.description: The provider's opaque identifier, used to start a sign-in flow for this provider.

name.description: The tenant-chosen display name of the provider, meant to be shown on the sign-in screen.

protocol.description: The protocol the provider's sign-in entry uses

AuthnTokenJWK.description: One public JSON Web Key. The published keys carry `kty`, `kid`, `alg` and `use`; the remaining members depend on the key type: an EC key carries `crv`, `x` and `y`, an RSA key carries `n` and `e`.

kty.description: The key type, for example EC or RSA

kid.description: The RFC 7638 thumbprint of the public key

alg.description: The signature algorithm the key signs and verifies with

crv.description: The curve of an EC key; only P-256 is supported, so this is `P-256`.

x.description: The x coordinate of an EC public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

y.description: The y coordinate of an EC public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

n.description: The modulus of an RSA public key, at least 2048 bits, base64url-encoded without padding.

e.description: The public exponent of an RSA public key, base64url-encoded without padding.

AuthnTokenJWKS.description: The public key set published on `GET /auth/jwks.json`, served as `application/jwk-set+json`. It holds the public half of every key loaded at startup and no private field.

keys.description: Every configured key's public JWK; the set is never empty.

AuthnTokenOAuthError.description: The failure body of RFC 6749 §5.2, which the token and revocation endpoints answer in place of the entry point's problem+json. Its only member is `error`; no `error_description` accompanies it.

error.description: The machine-readable failure code, one of `invalid_request`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type` and `temporarily_unavailable`.

AuthnTokenResponse.description: The success body of `POST /auth/token`, per RFC 6749 §5.1. A `client_credentials` response carries no `refresh_token`.

access_token.description: The signed access token: a compact JWT, presented as a `Bearer` credential.

expires_in.description: The access token's remaining lifetime in whole seconds

refresh_token.description: Present only for the refresh_token grant

AuthzAdminBindingView.description: One role binding: an account holds a role within a tenant.

tenant.description: The tenant the binding belongs to.

account.description: The account the role is bound to.

role.description: The role bound to the account.

granted_at.description: When the binding was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

AuthzAdminGrantView.description: One permission grant of a role: the (resource, action) pair the policy engine matches on.

tenant.description: The tenant the grant belongs to.

resource.description: The resource the grant matches on.

action.description: The action the grant matches on.

created_at.description: When the grant was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

permission.description: The permission name as the catalog declares it, for example authn.tenant.access. Only the authn.* permissions are the same vocabulary as authn.Action and carry its string; a permission outside it, such as authz.role.read, has no corresponding authn.Action.

AuthzAdminRoleView.description: One role of a tenant as the role routes report it.

tenant.description: The tenant the role belongs to.

role.description: The role name within the tenant.

builtin.description: True for a builtin role: the management face can neither rewrite nor remove it, nor change its grants. The mark is set by the host that seeds the policy data and is never cleared.

description_key.description: The i18n key of the role's description text; stored as given and not resolved by this surface.

created_at.description: When the role was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

AuthzAdminRoleWrite.description: The body of a role write: the role's description key only. The builtin mark is not part of the body; a member sent under that name reaches nothing.

description_key.description: The i18n key of the role's description text. It is stored as given and not resolved by this surface.

FeatureBoardDocument.description: The feature document: the feature names this process serves, decided by the assembly at start and frozen before the first request, so it is the same for every caller and every tenant. The object is extensible — a field added beside features is a compatible change — and carries no feature of its own.

features.description: The feature names this process serves, ascending and without repetition. Each name answers whether a frontend surface the caller's build carries is served here; the response carries no configuration value, method descriptor or rendering description.

NotificationMessage.description: One in-app message as the inbox shows it. The title and body arrive already rendered, and the bookkeeping columns — tenant, recipient, dedupe key, expiry and update time — are not part of this view.

id.description: The message identifier; it is the value the per-message mark-read route takes.

type_key.description: The notification type key the message was dispatched under, shaped like <module>.<entity>.<action>.

group.description: The group the message was filed under; the listing filters on it. Empty when the message was filed under none.

title.description: The rendered title, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

body.description: The rendered body, in the language the delivery pipeline rendered it in.

params.description: The type's parameters after the allow-list filter, as an opaque JSON object the client renders into the message; null when the message carries none.

link.description: The optional navigation target; the empty string when the message carries none.

read_at.description: The first-read instant as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while the message is unread, and never rewritten once set.

created_at.description: When the message was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

NotificationPreference.description: One row of the caller's preference matrix: a notification type and the channels that type's dispatches would go out under for the caller.

type_key.description: The notification type key this row describes.

group.description: The type's grouping label, copied from its declaration.

channels.description: The caller's effective channel set for the type: the stored channels when a row exists, otherwise the type's default channels; a type that cannot be unsubscribed always carries its default channels.

explicit.description: True when the channels came from a stored row, false when they are the type's default channels

NotificationSetPreferenceRequest.description: The body of a single-channel preference update.

enabled.description: The target state of the channel; a body naming none is told apart from one naming false

NotificationType.description: One notification type as declared by the business module that owns it; the taxonomy is fixed at startup and read-only for the life of the process.

key.description: The globally unique type key; two modules declaring one key fail the process startup.

group.description: The grouping label the declaring module assigns to the type.

default_channels.description: The channels a recipient gets for this type when no preference row is stored. Non-empty, free of duplicates, and drawn from the channel set.

unsubscribable.description: Whether a recipient may change this type's channel set. False means writes answer 409 and the effective set is always default_channels.

recipient_visible_params.description: The parameter names the declaring module allows to be shown to the recipient. This module stores and returns the list but does not interpret it.

ObjectstoreDeclaration.description: The body of a declaration: what the caller states before any byte is stored. size and content_type are required; name and checksum_sha256 may be omitted.

name.description: An optional label for the object; normalized before storing, and omitted or empty stores an empty name

size.description: The object's size in bytes; must be positive, and the upload's byte count must equal it exactly. A declaration without a positive size is refused whole.

content_type.description: The media type the bytes will carry; must be non-blank. The upload records it as the object's mime.

checksum_sha256.description: The declared SHA-256 as 64 hex digits; empty declares no checksum

ObjectstoreObject.description: One object as the routes expose it: the values observed by the last upload plus the row's timestamps. It never carries the internal storage key, and every instant is UTC.

id.description: The object's identifier, minted at declaration; every other object route takes it in the path.

name.description: The declared label, normalized once when the object was created; empty when none was declared or it normalized to nothing

state.description: The lifecycle state: pending after declaration, uploaded once bytes are stored, completed after the completion call, deleted once tombstoned. A deleted object reads as 404 on every route except delete.

size.description: The observed byte count recorded by the last upload; zero until the first upload lands.

mime.description: The content type recorded by the last upload, taken from the declared content_type; empty until the first upload lands.

checksum_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the stored bytes as 64 lowercase hex digits, computed during the last upload; empty until the first upload lands.

expires_at.description: When a completed object will be swept into deleted, written from object-ttl at completion; absent when no lifetime is configured, so the object does not expire.

created_at.description: When the object was declared, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

updated_at.description: When the row last changed, whether by declaration, upload, completion or deletion, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

OpsDocument.description: The merged OpenAPI document: the version it declares, its info section, every merged path, the components its fragments declared, and x-fragments naming each source

OpsHealth.description: The liveness response body: a single status field, always ok on a process that can answer.

status.description: The literal the liveness route writes; a live process always answers ok

OpsReadiness.description: The readiness response body, carrying the verdict and, when it is unavailable, one line per part that failed.

status.description: ready when every part answered, unavailable otherwise

failures.description: One line per part that failed; absent when the verdict is ready

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

SettingsAdminSetting.description: One declared setting item as this management surface shows it, on the selected layer. The declaration fields come from the key table; written, has_row and value come from that layer's rows and from the resolved read. Every value-bearing field is text in the declared type's own form, so a duration reads as "5m0s" rather than as a count of nanoseconds.

key.description: The full setting key: the declaring module's namespace joined with the item's own segment by a dot.

namespace.description: The module that declared the item

type.description: The declared type's name as reflection reports it, such as `string`, `int`, `bool` or `time.Duration`; the item's values are stored and rendered in that type's text form.

description.description: The human-readable text the declaring module gave the item.

domain.description: The declared rule over the item's values, empty when every value of the type is admitted

sensitive.description: Whether the item is a credential. A sensitive item's default is empty and its written and value carry a fixed mask string; has_row still reports whether the layer holds a row.

default.description: The declared default in the declared type's text form, empty for a sensitive item

written.description: The text the selected layer holds, the mask string for a sensitive item

has_row.description: Whether the selected layer holds a row for the item. For a non-sensitive item, written is empty both when no row is held and when the row's text is empty; a sensitive item's written is the mask string whether or not a row exists.

value.description: The text the item resolves to after the three-level fallback, the mask string for a sensitive item

SmsAdminApproval.description: The vendor's review verdict on one template in one language.

state.description: The verdict in this capability's own vocabulary: pending, approved, rejected or withdrawn; an empty string means a review this process does not track. The vendor's raw status numbers are never exposed.

reason.description: The vendor's own explanation, present when it turned the template down and it gave one; omitted otherwise.

SmsAdminRegister.description: The body of a registration: a template whose vendor code the operator already has.

name.description: The logical template name to take up; required and non-empty, and the name a caller will later send under. A language the name already holds is a 409.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them.

codes.description: The vendor's template code per language, keyed by locale. Every language named starts pending, and the template starts enabled.

SmsAdminSubmission.description: The body of a submission: a template handed to the vendor for review.

name.description: The logical template name the submission creates; required and non-empty.

content.description: The template body, written with ${name} placeholders naming the entries of params. The carrier rewrites them into the vendor's own syntax, in params order.

kind.description: What the template is for, in the shared vocabulary: verification, notification or marketing. The carrier maps it to the vendor's spelling.

locale.description: The language this submission is for, opaque to the capability. A vendor approves per language, so one submission yields one code for one language.

params.description: The parameter names content substitutes, in the order the template expects them.

remark.description: A note for the vendor's reviewer; may be empty.

SmsAdminTemplate.description: One template as the management surface reports it: its logical name, its source, its ordered parameter names, the languages it holds a code for, the vendor's review per language, whether sends are allowed, and its write counters. It carries no vendor code.

name.description: The logical template name a caller sends under; the management routes address a template by it.

source.description: Where the template came from: config for one read from the configuration, runtime for one this process created. A config template is read-only at runtime, always enabled, and carries no approvals and no version.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them; a positional vendor lays values out in this order.

locales.description: The languages the template holds a vendor code for. A code is what a send needs but not the whole of what it needs: a runtime template sends only while it is enabled and the language's vendor review is approved, and every language a runtime template names starts pending review whether the template was registered or submitted, so this list normally includes languages that cannot be sent in yet. A configured template is always enabled and its review is not tracked, so each language it holds a code for can be sent in.

approvals.description: The vendor's review verdict per language, keyed by locale; a vendor approves a template per language. A configured template carries an empty object because this process does not track its review.

enabled.description: Whether a message may go out under the template. A configured template is always enabled; a runtime template's value is set by the enable route and is independent of the vendor's review.

version.description: The number of writes this runtime record has taken, used as the optimistic-concurrency condition; 0 for a configured template, which has no version.

created_at.description: When the record was first written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

TenantAdminTenant.description: One tenant as the management routes render it: the identifier, the alias and the state.

id.description: The tenant's identifier, the natural key the roster keys the row by.

alias.description: The alias the request surface addresses the tenant by.

status.description: The tenant's state: active is served, disabled is not.

TenantAdminTenantRegistration.description: A registration: the identifier to insert and the alias to give it. The state is not part of it, because a registered tenant starts active.

id.description: The identifier to register; the roster refuses one it already holds.

alias.description: The alias to give the tenant; the roster refuses one another tenant already holds.

WorkspacePersonalReply.description: The answer to a successful ensure: the caller's personal tenant and whether this call registered it.

created.description: Whether this call registered the tenant

WorkspacePersonalTenant.description: The personal tenant the ensure names. It carries no display name: the frontend renders the personal label from the kind.

id.description: The tenant identifier, derived deterministically from the account identifier: the fixed prefix "personal-" followed by the account identifier, the same string the alias carries. The scoped tables hold it, so it takes no phone number, display name or other personal data, and it does not change with the request language

alias.description: The request-surface name, equal to the identifier for a personal tenant

kind.description: The tenant kind; the frontend renders the personal label from it
